meta.title: Myth Juice ep02 pronunciation lexicon (Rodney, ElevenLabs eleven_v4, English)
meta.episode: ep02 Hawaiʻi drained (launch title "Why Can't You See Most of Hawaii? (Look Down)")
meta.status: DRAFT: not yet test-rendered, not yet checked on wehewehe.org, not yet heard by a Hawaiian speaker. Do not render the full narration until open_items 1-3 are closed.
how_to_use: Script text (captions, SRT, labels, description) always uses "spelling": ʻokina = U+02BB (never an apostrophe or U+2018), kahakō = precomposed NFC vowels (Ā ā Ē ē Ī ī Ō ō Ū ū).

The TTS text (segments.json for engine/tools/tts.py) uses "tts" in place of the spelling, and only there (PLAYBOOK_craft section 11: respell only in the VO text, never on screen). Never put U+02BB or kahakō vowels in TTS text unless the test render shows the voice handles them.

Every "tts" value has the same number of space-separated tokens as "spelling", so word timings line up one to one. tts.py builds timing.json words from the TTS text, and make_srt.py and asr_check.py read those words, so map each timing word through caption_map before make_srt.py and before asr_check.py (a small mapping step; it does not exist yet, see open_items).
Possessives keep the respelling and add 's ("kee-lao-WAY-ah's" maps to "Kīlauea's"; caption_map already holds the 's forms).
No break, bracket or phoneme tags in TTS text (PLAYBOOK_craft section 11). The IPA fields are the reference for the listener and the QC pass, not input to the voice.

ALL-CAPS labels keep both marks: MOLOKAʻI, LĀNAʻI, KĪLAUEA, KAMAʻEHUAKANALOA. Anton and Barlow Condensed 800 in engine/www/fonts contain U+02BB and all kahakō capitals and lower-case vowels (checked with fontTools on 2026-11-08), but only if the page loads both the latin and the latin-ext woff2 subsets.

Give the long names (Kamaʻehuakanaloa, Papahānaumokuākea, Mokumanamana) their own take at speed about 0.9, with a pause of about 0.4 s before them and no other new proper noun within 10 s (PLAYBOOK section 5: at most 3 new proper nouns in any 10 s).

respelling_key.ao: /aʊ/ as in Mao or cow (used instead of "ow", which a voice can read as mow /moʊ/)
respelling_key.CAPS: the stressed syllable (two CAPS syllables = two stresses)
respelling_key.hyphen: syllable break; a hyphen between two vowels where the spelling has an ʻokina stands for the glottal catch

test_protocol: 1. Render every narration-use entry in a neutral carrier sentence from the script, three variants each: plain ASCII spelling, tts, first tts_alt; Rodney, eleven_v4, the planned stability/style; same speed as its script take.

2. Run asr_check.py (small.en and medium.en) on each test clip; a variant passes when the heard word is in asr_accept or is the closest English approximation. ASR cannot judge Hawaiian vowels or glottal stops, so it only catches gross errors.
3. A person listens (the owner, ideally with a Hawaiian speaker); agents never claim an ear verdict (PLAYBOOK_production section 16). Write the chosen variant into a new "locked_tts" field per entry.

4. Only then generate the narration. After TTS, map timing.json words through caption_map, then run make_srt.py and asr_check.py; finish with the full phone-speaker listen before upload (niche report 4.5).
method_and_sources: Spellings: as the agencies write them (USGS/HVO, NPS, USFWS, NOAA, UH, Papahānaumokuākea; ledger C4-14 and the other ledger entries cited per name).

Native IPA: Wikipedia article IPA (which cites or follows Pukui & Elbert) and Wiktionary haw-IPA (stress units such as Molo+kaʻi, kahoʻo+lawe, Kana+loa); Papahānaumokuākea's own respelling for that name.

Rule-derived entries (status "rule-derived"): stress from Hawaiian stress units (stress on the second-to-last mora of each unit; long vowels and diphthongs count as two moras), per Wikipedia Hawaiian phonology (Pukui & Elbert 1986, Elbert & Pukui 1979). That article warns that stress in words longer than three moras is not fully predictable, so every rule-derived entry needs the dictionary check.

wehewehe.org, ulukau.org, puke.ulukau.org and trussel2.com (the Pukui-Elbert and Place Names of Hawaiʻi texts) returned HTTP 403 browser challenges to scripted requests on 2026-11-08, and the archive.org copy of Place Names of Hawaii (1974) is access-restricted. They were not bypassed. No entry is verified on wehewehe yet.
decisions_for_script_lock: Mauna Kea (USGS, matches Mauna Loa and the tags; recommended) or Maunakea (UH / Center for Maunakea Stewardship): one form everywhere.
Nihoa (USFWS, Papahānaumokuākea, ledger; recommended) or Nīhoa (Wikipedia, after Pukui-Elbert nīhoa).
La Pérouse (ledger) or La Perouse (USFWS, Wikipedia) on the label.
open_items: 1. A person opens wehewehe.org in a normal browser, looks up each entry in Place Names of Hawaiʻi and Pukui-Elbert, and records agreement or the correction (first the critical and high entries, then every rule-derived one).
2. Test-render per test_protocol (needs the ElevenLabs key and the owner's OK to spend credits) and lock the variants.
3. Hawaiian-speaker or owner listen on the locked variants (niche report 5.2.4: the single biggest trust risk for this film).
4. Add a caption_map step (timing.json words to captions) in front of make_srt.py and asr_check.py.
no_entry_needed_english: Hawaiian (English adjective, no ʻokina: "Hawaiian monk seal", "Hawaiian Deep")

excluded.Laupāhoehoe: cut from the film (brief section 4, must-fix 5)
excluded.Pailolo, Kalohi, ʻAlenuihāhā, ʻAlalākeik: saddle measurements only (ledger C12-03); add an entry if any is labelled or narrated
excluded.Pihemanu, Mokupāpapa, Kauō: alternative Hawaiian names of Midway, Kure and Laysan; not planned

entries.where_in_film: First spoken word (0:00) and throughout; labels, captions, description
entries.ipa_target: /həˈwaɪ.ʔi/ (three syllables, light glottal catch before the last "ee")
entries.note: Plain ASCII "Hawaii" is usually spoken correctly by English voices; use "hah-WHY-ee" only if the test render gives two syllables ("huh-WHY"). Possessive: "Hawaii's" / "hah-WHY-ee's" maps to "Hawaiʻi's". w and v are both correct after a (free variation); keep w for this film. Captions and labels always "Hawaiʻi" with U+02BB. The English adjective "Hawaiian" has no ʻokina and needs no respelling. Launch title stays as approved (packaging section 9).

entries.where_in_film: 0:14-0:20 Maui Nui hero line (packaging promise: name Maui, Molokaʻi, Lānaʻi by 0:14); Ch4 time machine
entries.note: English voices normally say it right; fall back to "MAO-ee" ("ao" as in Mao/cow). Never "MOW" (could be read as mow-the-lawn).

entries.where_in_film: 0:14 hero shot label if a name is shown for the joined island; the narration says "three islands become one"
entries.note: Name given by geologists (Wikipedia); nui = big. Two TTS tokens map to two caption words.

entries.where_in_film: 0:20 "Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi were one island" (packaging condition by 0:14-0:20)
entries.note: The ʻokina splits "ka" and "i": four syllables, never "MOLLY-kai" or "Molo-KAI" with an "eye" diphthong (the most common error). Wiktionary stress units Molo+kaʻi.

entries.where_in_film: 0:20 Maui Nui line; label in the -400 ft shot
entries.note: Long first ā, then "NAH-ee" with a glottal break. Never "luh-NYE" (the anglicised form Wikipedia also lists).

entries.where_in_film: -400 ft shot: the separate, dimmed island; ledger C12-06 says not needed in narration
entries.note: Stress units kahoʻo+lawe (Wiktionary). "lawe" ends in a pure e, not "way". v and w both correct after a. If narrated, say it in its own short sentence (4 names in 10 s would break the proper-noun cap).

entries.where_in_film: 0:47 1975 beat ("below Kīlauea", optional), 3:10 "Kīlauea's south flank", Ch6 Kamaʻehuakanaloa placement
entries.note: "lao" = "lau" as in cow. Avoid the anglicised "KILL-uh-WAY-uh". Possessive: "kee-lao-WAY-ah's" maps to "Kīlauea's".

entries.where_in_film: Ch3 3:55 "33,500 FT" beat, 4:30 summit-road gag (never a punchline at the summit), 4:40 "Mauna Kea isn't the giant"
entries.note: "Mauna" rhymes with "how-nah", not "MAW-nuh" (anglicised form). Spelling decision open: USGS "Mauna Kea" vs UH/Center for Maunakea Stewardship "Maunakea" (same sound); pick one for every label, caption and the description at script lock. Recommendation: "Mauna Kea" to match "Mauna Loa" and the search tags. If "Maunakea" is chosen, the TTS stays two tokens and caption_tokens must map both to one word (merge in make_srt).

entries.where_in_film: Ch3 4:40 "Mauna Loa, the largest active volcano"; PAYOFF 11:10-11:45 "Measured from its true base, Mauna Loa is about fifty-six thousand feet tall"
entries.note: The payoff name: lock the variant on a separate test render before any narration run, and give the payoff take its own ASR check. "Loa" is two syllables (LOH-ah), never one.

entries.where_in_film: Ch3 3:30 "five volcanoes merge" labels
entries.note: Long ā carries the stress. Words over three moras have unpredictable stress, so confirm on wehewehe (Place Names of Hawaiʻi).

entries.where_in_film: Ch3/Ch4 age line ("its oldest volcano above water, Kohala", ledger C4-02)
entries.note: Three moras, stress on "ha" by rule. Plain spelling may work; test.

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 age caveat (submarine volcano older than Kohala); label only if shown
entries.note: No published IPA found; stress from stress units mā + hukona. Check on wehewehe before use.

entries.where_in_film: Ch1 optional drill line ("Under Hilo, a drill found...", ledger C12-11); thumbnail camera reference
entries.note: Always respell: English voices often say "HY-loh".

entries.where_in_film: 0:47-1:10 1975 story beat ("At Halapē, a beach campsite on that coast, campers were asleep", ledger C12-13)
entries.note: Spelling with kahakō per USGS Volcano Watch 2025. The final long ē is stressed (stress units hala + pē). Solemn beat: speed about 0.9.

entries.where_in_film: Ch1/Ch2 "Hilina Slump" label on Kīlauea's south flank, if shown (the brief keeps the term off narration)
entries.note: Three moras, stress on "li" by rule. "Slump" is jargon; prefer "south flank" on screen.

entries.where_in_film: 1:20 gag and T9 hook: "the Pali Lookout"; pinned comment
entries.note: pali = cliff. Never "PAL-ee" or "PAY-lee". Official site name: Nuʻuanu Pali State Wayside.

entries.where_in_film: Ch2 Pali Lookout label ("Nuʻuanu Pali"), Nuʻuanu slide debris field; Ch4 Oʻahu callback
entries.note: Four syllables with a glottal break between "noo" and "oo". The film never needs the word "slide" with the name: the ledger narrates "the volcano that built eastern Oʻahu".

entries.where_in_film: Ch2 "the Koʻolau cliffs" / the volcano that built eastern Oʻahu
entries.note: koʻolau = windward. Glottal break between "koh" and "oh"; "lau" as in cow.

entries.where_in_film: Ch2 (eastern Oʻahu, the debris field), Ch4 time machine
entries.note: Three moras, stress on "ʻa" by rule; glottal catch before AH. Plain "Oahu" is usually fine; respelling guarantees the break.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 "Midway lies about thirteen hundred miles northwest of Honolulu" (ledger C5-20, optional)
entries.note: Plain spelling is fine; the respelling gives the purer local "o" vowels.

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 time machine: "Older still: Kauaʻi, carved into canyons"
entries.note: Wikipedia respelling "kah-WAH-ee". Never "KOW-eye" (the anglicised form).

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 time-machine flight past Kauaʻi (label only; not in the ledger narration)
entries.note: Two separate "ee" sounds with a glottal break, then "how".

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 7:00 human beat: "Seven million years in, it's a sliver of rock. And people lived here."
entries.note: Spelling decision: USFWS, Papahānaumokuākea and the ledger write "Nihoa"; Wikipedia moved to "Nīhoa" after Pukui-Elbert "nīhoa" (toothed, jagged). Recommendation: label "NIHOA" as the agencies do; the sound is the same either way (stress on HOH).

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 flight between Nihoa and Lalo (Necker Island); label only
entries.note: Stress units moku + mana + mana. If narrated, one take on its own at speed about 0.95.

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 7:30 label "LALO (FRENCH FRIGATE SHOALS)" (ledger C4-08); narration says "French Frigate Shoals"
entries.note: Hawaiian name of French Frigate Shoals (NOAA Fisheries). Two moras, stress on the first.

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 7:30 "La Pérouse Pinnacle, its last tooth" (ledger C4-08)
entries.note: Named after the French navigator (1786 near-wreck). Label "LA PÉROUSE PINNACLE" (ledger); USFWS and Wikipedia also write "La Perouse" without the accent. Two TTS tokens map to "La" and "Pérouse".

entries.where_in_film: Reserve line only (ledger C4-15, Gardner Pinnacles)
entries.note: Stress units pū + hā + honu. Not in the planned narration.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 8:00 "Most of the world's Laysan albatrosses nest here" (ledger C5-08)
entries.ipa_native: en /ˈlaɪ.sɑːn/ (Merriam-Webster via Wikipedia); Hawaiian name Kauō [kɐwˈoː]
entries.note: An English bird and island name, not Hawaiian; no diacritics. Check the plain spelling first.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 9:55 "This is Kure, the last atoll in the chain" (ledger C5-17b)
entries.note: Not "cure" and not "kyoor". No diacritics (Western name).

entries.where_in_film: Optional Hawaiian label beside KURE
entries.note: Stress units hō + lani + kū; main stress unconfirmed.

entries.where_in_film: Optional Hawaiian label beside MIDWAY
entries.note: Morpheme split not confirmed; check wehewehe before any use.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 9:30 wreck geography (the wrecks lie inside the monument); description and credits
entries.meaning: Papahānaumoku and Wākea, the earth mother and sky father (official site)
entries.note: The monument's own guide: "Pa-pa-hah-now-mo-koo-ah-keh-ah". Parts: Papa (earth mother), hānau (birth), moku (island), ākea (wide). If narrated, give it its own take at speed about 0.9 and no other proper noun within 10 s.

entries.where_in_film: Ch6 10:15 "a young volcano is growing. Its name is Kamaʻehuakanaloa." (ledger C6-01); label
entries.ipa_native: haw [ˌkɐməˌʔehuwəˌkɐnəˈlowə] (rule-derived from Kama + ʻehu + a + Kanaloa)
entries.note: HVO: "reddish child of Kanaloa", renamed from Lōʻihi in July 2021 by the Hawaiʻi Board on Geographic Names. Glottal break before EH. The longest name in the film: put it at the end of its sentence, in its own take at speed about 0.9, with a 0.4 s pause before it; hold the label on screen for the whole word. The third alt is two tokens: if used, map both tokens to the one caption word in make_srt.

entries.where_in_film: Ch6 optional "once called Lōʻihi" (the name viewers may know; Galilei commenters asked for "Lōʻihi")
entries.note: Former name (means "long"). If used, say "once called Lōʻihi" after the new name, never instead of it.

entries.where_in_film: Only if the narration explains the new name
entries.note: A major Hawaiian god; respectful, no jokes on this word.

entries.where_in_film: Ch4 time machine, Maui label (East Maui volcano) if shown
entries.note: Final long ā stressed.

entries.where_in_film: Mauna Kea summit cone; only if a label is needed. Never a punchline, no figure or car on it (ledger C3-09)
entries.note: Stress units puʻu + wē + kiu; check before use.

entries.where_in_film: Ch6 optional before the payoff: "the sea arch at Hōlei ... collapsed into the ocean" (ledger C6-10)
entries.ipa_native: haw [ˈhoːˈlei] (rule-derived: two heavy syllables, both stressed)
entries.note: Even stress on both syllables (long ō, then the "ei" diphthong). Spelling with kahakō per NPS.

entries.where_in_film: Only if the 1975 quake is named ("the Kalapana earthquake"); the planned line does not name it
entries.note: Stress units kala + pana.

entries.where_in_film: 0:25 suitcase gag sits on the ʻAuʻau Channel floor (ledger C12-03); label only if the channel is named
entries.note: Two "ow" (cow) syllables with glottal stops; a label is safer than narrating it.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 9:30 "Three of those wrecks have been found: Yorktown, Kaga and Akagi" (ledger C5-13)
entries.note: Hard g. War-grave beat: neutral tone, music down, no gags.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 9:30 wreck list (ledger C5-13)
entries.note: Hard g ("ghee"), never "ah-KAH-jee". Same tone rule as Kaga.

entries.where_in_film: Not narrated: the plan shows only the three found wrecks (ledger C5-13)
entries.note: Do not say "still lost" or "never found" (ledger C5-13).

entries.where_in_film: Not narrated (ledger C5-13)
entries.note: Same rule as Sōryū.

entries.where_in_film: Ch5 10:05 "all the way to Kamchatka, where a deep-sea trench is swallowing them" (ledger C5-18)
entries.note: The usual English form is correct here; the respelling is only a fallback.

entries.where_in_film: Not narrated: the ledger shows only "TRENCH" on screen (C5-18)
entries.note: Reserve only.

entries.where_in_film: Hand-off line names only "Louisiana"; end-screen element shows the video's own title
